title: External secret providers: the seam where a credential enters
note: A provider is the only place in the package that reads a credential from outside, so every refusal on it is load-bearing in a way an ordinary parser's is not. P1-P6 attack the file provider's own checks: the name rule that keeps an id from becoming a path, the newline handling that would otherwise silently corrupt a token, and the byte-level checks that decide whether a value can survive being used at all. P7-P9 attack the distinction between 'the store is not mounted' and 'the store has no such secret', which sends an operator to the right place or the wrong one. P10-P16 attack the store's provisioning path: the duplicate check that has to come BEFORE the read, the type checks that keep the value zeroable and the provenance honest, the assert_clean that stops a describe() carrying the credential into the log, and the all-or-nothing rules -- an empty load reporting success is this repository's oldest defect and P15 puts it back.

mutations.name: P1_any_name_is_a_secret_id
mutations.rationale: the id becomes a filename, so '../../etc/shadow' reaches the path layer and the refusal depends entirely on a module this one does not own

mutations.name: P2_the_name_rule_is_not_consulted
mutations.find: if not isinstance(secret_id, str) or not _PROVIDER_ID.match(secret_id):
mutations.rationale: same escape as P1, by the other route: the pattern is still correct and nothing asks it

mutations.name: P3_no_newline_is_stripped
mutations.rationale: every editor and every echo appends one, so the credential authenticates nowhere and the byte that broke it is invisible in any log

mutations.name: P4_all_trailing_newlines_are_stripped
mutations.rationale: a value that legitimately ends in a newline is silently altered; stripping once is a documented format rule, stripping greedily is data loss

mutations.name: P5_a_short_value_is_accepted
mutations.rationale: an empty or two-byte value registers, cannot be redacted from output without corrupting it, and an empty file becomes a 'successfully loaded' credential

mutations.name: P6_undecodable_bytes_are_accepted
mutations.rationale: the failure moves from load time to reveal() -- inside a run, under a grant, at the one call that needed the credential

mutations.name: P7_a_nul_byte_is_accepted
mutations.rationale: the value is silently truncated wherever it meets a C string, and the truncated form is what gets sent

mutations.name: P8_a_missing_root_looks_like_a_missing_secret
mutations.rationale: an unmounted secrets volume reports 'no such secret', and the operator goes looking for a key that was never the problem

mutations.name: P9_a_held_root_is_closed_by_every_fetch
mutations.rationale: the context manager stops meaning anything: the second fetch inside a with-block operates on a closed descriptor

mutations.name: P10_the_duplicate_check_happens_after_the_read
mutations.rationale: a credential this process has already decided it will not store is fetched into memory anyway

mutations.name: P11_a_str_value_is_stored
mutations.find:
if not isinstance(buf, bytearray):
            raise ProviderError(
mutations.rationale: the store's zeroing becomes decorative: a str cannot be wiped, and forget() would silently leave the plaintext behind

mutations.name: P12_anything_shaped_like_a_provider_is_one
mutations.find:
if not isinstance(provider, SecretProvider):
            raise ProviderError(
mutations.rationale: provenance recorded in the log is whatever describe() felt like returning, from an object with no contract behind it

mutations.name: P13_the_description_is_logged_unchecked
mutations.rationale: 'https://user:TOKEN@host/' is how half the world configures a client, and this writes it into the append-only log

mutations.name: P14_a_refused_description_leaves_the_secret_registered
mutations.rationale: the provisioning failed and the credential is in the store anyway, with no record that it ever arrived

mutations.name: P15_provisioning_nothing_succeeds
mutations.rationale: the vacuous-success defect, restored: a deployment step that loaded no credentials is indistinguishable from one that worked

mutations.name: P16_a_failed_load_leaves_half_a_credential_set
mutations.rationale: the run starts, does some of its work and fails at the one call that needed the secret that was missing

mutations.name: P17_the_mapping_provider_hands_out_its_own_buffer
mutations.rationale: the store zeroes what it is given, so the provider's copy is destroyed by the first load and every later one returns zeros

mutations.name: P18_duplicate_ids_are_reported_as_a_provider_fault
mutations.rationale: the second load fails as already-registered, which reads as the secret source misbehaving rather than the caller passing the same id twice
